author: Forbes
description:
With over $93 billion in loan and lease balances and relationships across roughly 75% of U.S. franchised dealerships, Chase Auto operates behind the scenes of nearly every corner of the automotive ecosystem. Forbes Cars & Bikes Contributor Scotty Reiss sits down with Leslie Wims-Morris, CEO of Chase Auto, as Leslie explains how Chase acts as the private-label captive finance partner for brands ranging from Subaru, Rivian, and Tesla to Jaguar Land Rover, Maserati, Aston Martin, and McLaren—and how AI is about to replace the traditional five-dealership shopping trip.

author: Forbes
description:
Sweeping changes to Formula 1’s technical regulations resulted in dramatically different car designs for 2026. Off the track, the series is undergoing a similarly radical transformation.

Just 12 months ago, Mercedes’ billionaire team principal, Toto Wolff, agreed to sell a minority stake in the team at an approximately $6 billion valuation—already a sign of major growth for the sport, at roughly six times the team’s estimated price tag from 2019. Today, the deal looks like a bargain. Forbes now values the Mercedes team at $9.2 billion—up 53% in a year—putting the Silver Arrows on a tier with the top half of the NFL, the NBA’s three most valuable teams and European soccer’s Real Madrid.

And while that is unquestionably impressive acceleration, Mercedes is neither the most valuable team in F1—that would be Ferrari, at $9.5 billion—nor the fastest growing, a title that goes this year to Haas after an astonishing 87% increase in its valuation to $2.8 billion, from 2025’s $1.5 billion. Born in the Soviet Union before moving to Japan and eventually the U.S., Archetype AI CEO Ivan Poupyrev has been at the helm of tech innovation since the first wave of virtual reality.

Poupyrev sat down with Senior Editor Alex Knapp to discuss his work across companies like Google and Walt Disney, and how he is venturing into the physical AI space.
